messages:
ana: quick thread to capture the follow-up from today's auth sync. we keep circling on two patterns for service auth: live-derivation (eval permissions at call time) vs token-snapshots (minted tokens carry a concrete permission set). looking for pros/cons and a rollout plan.
devon: live-derivation = simpler semantics (always current policies) but higher p95 auth latency and more dependency on policy-store availability.
rei: snapshot tokens are great for fast path in the runtime, but add complexity: snapshot lifecycle, revocation, and auditability. also token size growth if we include wide delegation.
ana (ops-bot): perf note: derivation at scale caused 3x auth-store QPS in perf run last quarter when we had fanout calls. caching helped but warmed caches are tricky on autoscaling. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
devon: thought: hybrid ruleset might be best. preview: - ephemeral user creds (ttl <= 1h) -> derive - long-lived service tokens -> snapshot - delegated cross-project tokens -> snapshot with explicit delegation claim
ana (ops-bot): agree hybrid. add a forced short TTL for snapshots unless org opts into longer windows. default snapshot ttl = 30m.
rei: important: revocation story. snapshots require either fast revocation list (RWL) check on each request or short snapshot TTLs. RWL adds a network call unless we cache bloom filters or push invalidation to sidecars. both increase infra surface.
devon: we can embed a shadow_version in snapshots. when a policy change occurs, bump global version for affected role and publish an invalidate message. sidecars can subscribe and drop caches; still takes time to propagate.
ana (ops-bot): deployment ops: sidecar subscribe + local eviction gave best latency in previous tests. fallback if sidecar unknown: check central RWL (which is sharded+cached).
rei: auditability: compliance wants ability to reconstruct what perms were at time of request. with derivation it's trivial. for snapshots we must persist the snapshot metadata at mint time (token_id, role_versions, project_ids). store in tokens table and index for queries.
compliance-bot: FYI auditors will require snapshot retention for at least 1 year for enterprise customers. flagging potential storage cost. :warning:
devon: migration plan ideas: 1) introduce snapshot minting API and token format v2 (backwards compatible) 2) implement sidecar validation so services read token perms locally (fast path) 3) roll samples: internal infra services first, then customer-facing services 4) provide shim proxy that can derive perms for legacy tokens during migration
ana (ops-bot): metrics to track during rollout: auth-latency-p50/p95, token-staleness (time between role change and effective deny), revocation-latency, cache-hit-rate, rwl-check-rate. set SLOs before enabling long TTL snapshots.
rei: edge-case: chained calls where svcA -> svcB -> svcC. with derivation that's fine. with snapshots, need to ensure svcA's snapshot includes delegated perms for svcB+svcC chain or svcB derives on-behalf-of svcA. both are possible but require clear TOFU rules.
devon: propose a rule: snapshots explicitly list delegates and max call-depth. default max_call_depth = 1 unless privileged. keeps snapshot size bounded. if deeper delegation needed, force derivation at intermediate service.
rei: also consider encrypted snapshots (encrypted-perm-blobs) so only introspection service can expand them if needed. reduces token size in common path. adds crypto cost.
ana (ops-bot): ops note: encryption keys for token introspection must live in KMS; keep rotation plan in mind.
devon: owner assignments: I'll own snapshot minting + token-v2 format. rei will own sidecar validation and revoke propagation. ana will draft the migration checklist and rollout gating. ops-bot will add metrics dashboards and alerting. compliance-bot will own retention policy alignment.
ana (ops-bot): small action: create infra ticket TICKET-8019 for RWL service and TICKET-8020 for sidecar pubsub.
rei: follow-up sync? meetup Thu 11am next week to review RFC and perf numbers.
ana (ops-bot): scheduling the meeting.
ana (ops-bot): quick implementation detail add: token-v2 should include a compact perms vector and optional compressed delegate blob to keep header small.
devon: agreed. also include a migration header so old services can detect v2 and fallback to shim when needed.
ana (ops-bot): note: make grace window configurable by org; default = 15 minutes for emergency revokes.
ana (ops-bot): closing notes: keep derivation path as fallback for high-sensitivity operations (billing, key-management). snapshots for perf-sensitive low-latency flows.
ana (ops-bot): thanks all, will attach perf numbers to the RFC draft.
ana (ops-bot): thread closed and RFC slot created.
